title: Image Sharing Technologies and Reduction of Imaging Utilization: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
authors_or_organization: Vest JR, Jung HY, Ostrovsky A, Das LT, McGinty GB (Weill Cornell Medical College)
url: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4730956 (J Am Coll Radiol 2015;12(12 Pt B):1371-1379.e3; doi 10.1016/j.jacr.2015.09.014; PMID 26614882)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Not reported in material reviewed; authors declare no conflicts related to the material
limitations: Meta-analysis of 17 articles/42 studies, mostly cohort or cross-sectional without true pre/post or comparison group; I^2=98%; 'standard effect size' metric not translated into natural units; likely includes Lu 2012 and other primary studies also in the register, so not independent of them; does not assess clinician time/efficiency, satisfaction or cost.

title: Outcomes From Health Information Exchange: Systematic Review and Future Research Needs
authors_or_organization: Hersh WR, Totten AM, Eden KB, Devine B, Gorman P, Kassakian SZ, Woods SS, Daeges M, Pappas M, McDonagh MS (Pacific Northwest Evidence-based Practice Center, OHSU)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: AHRQ contract 290-2012-00014-I; companion to AHRQ Evidence Report No. 220
limitations: Read via automated extraction of PMC full text (final ~4% of page not processed); evidence rated low strength; primary studies overlap with other HIE reviews; no outcome on clinician review time.

title: The benefits of health information exchange: an updated systematic review
authors_or_organization: Menachemi N, Rahurkar S, Harle CA, Vest JR (Indiana University / Regenstrief Institute)
url: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7646861 (J Am Med Inform Assoc 2018;25(9):1259-1265; doi 10.1093/jamia/ocy035; PMID 29718258)
data_collection_dates: Literature 2014-2017 (combined with earlier Rahurkar et al. review for some analyses)
limitations: Vote-counting of analyses rather than pooled effect sizes; ~40% of analyses from a handful of New York HIEs; positive conclusions may reflect publication bias; outcomes are utilization/cost, not professional effort. Full text read via automated extraction; percentages partly derived by extraction tool.

title: Usage and effect of health information exchange: a systematic review
authors_or_organization: Rudin RS, Motala A, Goldzweig CL, Shekelle PG (RAND / VA)
limitations: Only the PubMed abstract was reviewed (RAND page returned 403; journal full text not accessed). Usage data come from 13 HIE organizations, 6 in New York; evidence rated low quality.

title: Does health information exchange reduce redundant imaging? Evidence from emergency departments
authors_or_organization: Lammers EJ, Adler-Milstein J, Kocher KE (Mathematica Policy Research; University of Michigan)
data_collection_dates: 2007-2010 (California and Florida State Emergency Department Databases)
limitations: Observational panel (ED fixed effects and trends); only abstract reviewed. HIE exposure is hospital participation (HIMSS data), not clinician use; repeat defined only across unaffiliated EDs within 30 days; two states, early HIE period.

title: Outside imaging in emergency department transfer patients: CD import reduces rates of subsequent imaging utilization
authors_or_organization: Sodickson A, Opraseuth J, Ledbetter S (Brigham and Women's Hospital)
data_collection_dates: Feb 1 - Aug 31, 2009; historical control Aug 2007 - Jan 2008
limitations: Single site; retrospective comparison of successful vs failed import (failure may correlate with patient/sending-hospital characteristics) plus historical control; only abstract reviewed; measures imaging counts within 24h, not clinician review time.

title: An empirical analysis of the financial benefits of health information exchange in emergency departments
url: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7784316 (J Am Med Inform Assoc 2015;22(6):1169-1172; doi 10.1093/jamia/ocv068; PMID 26117143)
limitations: Non-randomized shift-based assignment in one suburban ED over ~2 months; standard errors but no CIs; HIE queries performed by dedicated hired liaisons (so effect is of a staffed integration service, not routine clinician use); read via automated extraction of PMC text.

title: Impact of Electronic Information Exchange on Repeat Imaging During 30-Day Readmissions Among Medicare Beneficiaries
authors_or_organization: Turbow SD, Culler SD, Vaughan EC, Rask KJ, Perkins MM, Clevenger CK, Ali MK (Emory University)
data_collection_dates: 2018 Medicare MedPAR and Carrier files; AHA Annual Survey 2018 and IT Supplement 2017-2018
limitations: National cohort (observational). Exposure is hospital-reported HIE participation (AHA IT Supplement), not use at point of care; 16.3% of pairs missing HIE data; does not know whether images or only reports were shared; cannot separate appropriate from wasteful repeats.

title: The Role of Technology in Mortgage Lending (NBER Working Paper 24500; published Review of Financial Studies 2019)
authors_or_organization: Fuster A, Plosser M, Schnabl P, Vickery J (Federal Reserve Bank of New York; NYU Stern)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Authors include Federal Reserve Bank of New York staff; views not those of the Fed
limitations: Observational lender-type comparison (FinTech vs other lenders), not an intervention on data integration per se; FinTech bundles online application, electronic data verification, centralization and automation; WP version reviewed, published version may differ; consumer mortgages are highly standardized relative to project finance.

title: Inheriting Versus Developing Data Analytic Tests and Auditors' Professional Skepticism
authors_or_organization: Li X, Brazel JF, Gold A, Leiby J
url: https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-679X.70014 (Journal of Accounting Research 2026;64(2):885-922); press release https://news.ncsu.edu/2025/09/blind-spot-for-auditors/
limitations: Wiley full text returned 403; reviewed abstract excerpts (VU research portal, search snippets) and the NC State press release, which is the source of the percentage figures; cell sizes, test statistics and materials not verified. Hypothetical case experiment with 173 practitioners.

title: AI-Powered Spreading Transforms Lending Operations at Leading Global Bank (Spreadsmart case study)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Vendor-authored marketing case study about its own product
limitations: Vendor self-report; anonymous client; no baseline values, measurement method, time period or denominator; headline stat blocks rendered as '0 %' on page; selection and attribution limits.
